newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Racing for Costa Rican coffee, Beaujolais-style.
newsitem.headline: Racing for Costa Rican coffee, Beaujolais-style.

text.p: One French coffee roaster plans next year to expand on a Beaujolais Nouveau-style race that bids to get the first new harvest Costa Rican coffee beans from a top growing area into Parisian cups.

Using the principles of the feted French wine race, Kraft Jacobs Suchard launched "cafe primeur" this summer, starting a race to transport beans from the Tarrazu high-altitude mountain plantations, across the Atlantic, up the Seine and into Paris coffee pots.

"It was a big success," said Kraft general director Roland Monica, refering to the first cafe primeur of beans from the coffee zone just outside the capital city in this tiny Central American nation. "In 1997, we will do the same operation, but on a larger scale," he added.
Kraft is a unit of Phillip Morris Cos Inc.
